title: Yara and the Cipher Again
premise: Ansel Joubert, a private security contractor with a fabricated past and a go-bag always by the door, is hired to protect a nervous data-broker named Tomas Reyes. Mid-flight over the Atlantic, every record of the flight — manifests, transponder logs, even Ansel's own contract — evaporates from every database on earth. Stranded in Lisbon with a client who may be the target or the trigger, she discovers the vanished flight carried a cipher that can rewrite digital identity itself, and that her own polished lie is a thread someone wove into it years ago. Hunted by the agency that made her and the syndicate that wants the cipher, Ansel must trade the one secret worth killing for — the truth of who she was before she became Ansel — to save the found family she never meant to build. In the end she burns her old identity for good, exposes the agency's role in the vanishing, and chooses loyalty to the people who know her lie and love her anyway.
about_author: I. M. Joubert is the pen name of a former aviation-logistics analyst who spent a decade around charter flights, customs brokers, and people who preferred not to be named. They write thrillers about the paperwork of disappearance and the people caught inside it.

chapters.title: The Packed Bag
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. We meet her in a Lisbon safehouse: go-bag packed, three passports, a backstory rehearsed until it feels true. She takes a lucrative contract guarding Tomas Reyes, a data-broker flying to Washington. Emotional beat: controlled loneliness mistaken for freedom.

chapters.title: Client Nobody Trusts
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Pre-flight vetting: Reyes is paranoid, charming, and clearly terrified of someone specific. He hints he's carrying something 'heavier than money.' Ansel notices his fear matches her own tells. Beat: reluctant curiosity; two liars recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Wheels Up
chapters.summary: Alternating Ansel and Reyes POVs aboard the chartered jet. Small talk turns into an exchange of confessions neither fully means. Reyes says if anything happens, 'find the woman who answers to a name I'll give you.' Beat: fragile trust forming at 35,000 feet.

chapters.title: Vanishing Point
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Over the Atlantic, Reyes checks a terminal and goes white: the flight number no longer exists. No manifest, no transponder history, no contract naming Ansel. The plane keeps flying, but officially it never took off. Beat: vertigo — reality edited beneath them.

chapters.title: Forced Landing
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The pilot, spooked by garbled ATC silence, diverts back to Lisbon under a false callsign. On the tarmac, ground crew treat them like ghosts. Ansel's burner lights up: a message containing only her real, buried name. Beat: dread sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Name She Buried
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Ansel's POV. Ten years earlier: a recruit with a different name signs away her identity to a private intelligence outfit called Meridian. We learn her 'polished lie' was authored by Meridian itself. Beat: the past arriving as a bill due.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Hiding in a fisherman's flat, Reyes explains what the flight carried: a cipher that can forge or erase any digital identity — including Ansel's. He admits he stole it from Meridian. Beat: betrayal braided with understanding.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Answers
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Following Reyes's instruction, she contacts Nadia Okafor, a retired fixer who once ran Meridian's field agents. Nadia knows Ansel's real name and greets her like a daughter returning. Beat: first taste of belonging, immediately suspect.

chapters.title: Tail Lights
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. A Meridian wet team finds the safehouse. Ansel extracts Reyes through laundry lines and rooftops while Nadia stays behind to burn evidence. Beat: found family forged under fire; Nadia's sacrifice implied.

chapters.title: What the Flight Carried
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. In a tram depot, Reyes reveals the full stakes: Meridian plans to sell the cipher to a syndicate that will make witnesses, debts, and dissidents vanish wholesale. The vanished flight was a test run. Beat: personal stakes become moral ones.

chapters.title: Loyalty Audit
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Meridian's handler, Voss, reaches out: surrender Reyes and the cipher, and Ansel gets her old life back — records restored, name returned. She has twelve hours. Beat: the offer that makes her want to say yes.

chapters.title: Twelve Hours
chapters.summary: Split POV. Reyes sleeps; Ansel stands watch and interrogates herself. Nadia reappears, wounded but alive, and refuses to tell Ansel what to choose: 'Loyalty you're paid for isn't loyalty.' Beat: quiet before the storm; love without conditions.

chapters.title: The Broker's Confession
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Reyes admits he didn't just steal the cipher — he built its kill-switch, and only he can arm it. He also confesses he chose Ansel specifically because Meridian wrote her, making her the one guard they'd never suspect. Beat: trust tested and, painfully, kept.

chapters.title: Voss
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Inside Meridian's Lisbon station we see the machinery: the flight erased as a demonstration for buyers, Ansel designed as a deniable asset from day one. Voss genuinely believes he's saving order from chaos. Beat: chilling competence, humanized villainy.

chapters.title: Dead Drop
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel arranges a trade: the cipher's location for her original file. She plans to double-cross both sides, using the dead drop to trace the syndicate buyer. Beat: the liar running her most dangerous con yet.

chapters.title: Double Blind
chapters.summary: Alternating Ansel and Voss POVs at the exchange — a shuttered airport hangar. Both expected betrayal; the meeting collapses into gunfire when the syndicate arrives early to take everything. Beat: chaos as equalizer; alliances scrambled.

chapters.title: Runway Fire
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Hangar shootout becomes a chase across live taxiways. Reyes is taken; Nadia covers Ansel's escape and is gravely wounded. Ansel escapes with half the cipher key. Beat: cost of loyalty paid in blood.

chapters.title: The Trade Worth Killing For
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Cornered, Ansel offers Voss the only currency left: her true identity file — proof Meridian manufactured her, evidence that could unravel the agency publicly. Voss wants it destroyed; the syndicate wants it as leverage. Beat: she weaponizes her own erasure.

chapters.title: Kill-Switch
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV, captive. Forced to arm the cipher for the syndicate, Reyes instead triggers the kill-switch, corrupting the master copy as buyers watch their leverage dissolve. Beat: the mild man's quiet courage; the vault door swinging open.

chapters.title: Everything Vanishes
chapters.summary: Climax, Ansel's POV. With the cipher dying, Ansel broadcasts Meridian's files — including her own — to journalists and regulators worldwide. Voss confronts her on the tarmac of the same runway where the flight vanished; she chooses arrest-worthy exposure over a clean escape. Beat: truth chosen over survival.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Unrecorded
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. Weeks later: hearings begin, Voss detained, the syndicate scattered. Nadia recovers; Reyes testifies under protection. Ansel is officially a ghost again — but this time by her own hand, not Meridian's. Beat: grief and relief entwined.

chapters.title: Yara
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, final chapter. She unpacks the go-bag for the first time in ten years and lets Nadia and Reyes call her by the name she buried: Yara. No new contract, no packed bag, a table set for three. Beat: belonging earned, the lie finally set down.
